OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Sadiq Ali, a former Member of this House, on the 17th 
April, 2001, at the age of 91. 
Born in Udaipur in 1910, Shri Ali had his education at Maharana 
College, Udaipur and at Allahabad University, Allahabad. A staunch supporter 
of Gandhian values, Shri Ali joined the movement for freedohT*fn 1930. He 
also took an active part  in the Civil Disobedience Movement and Quit India 
Movement and was imprisoned on many occasions. He was associated with 
several Gandhian institutes, including the Gandhi Smarak Nidhi and the 
National Gandhi Memorial. He had several publications to his credit on 
Indian culture and socialist values. Th e distinguished legislative career of 
Shri Ali started with the membership of Provisional Parliament from 1950 to 
1952. He represented the State of Rajasthan in this House for two 
consecutive terms from November, 1958 to April, 1964 and from April, 1964 
to April, 1970. He also served as Governor of Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. 
He will always be remembered for his commitment to democratic values and 
traditions. 
In the passing away of Shri Sadiq Alif the country has lost a veteran 
freedom fighter, an eminent Parliamentarian, a great nationalist and an able 
administrator. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Sadiq Ali. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark 
of respect to the memory of the departed. 
{Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of 
the bereaved family our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.

ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS  
Houses constructed under Indira Awas Yojana 
*461.   SHRI  BACHANI  LEKHRAJ:   Will  the  Minister  of 
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government have conducted any review of houses 
constructed under the Indira Awas Yojana; 
(b) if so, the number of houses constructed during last year in Gujarat; 
(c) whether the Government are satisfi ed with the pace of construction 
of such houses; and 
(d) if not, the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. 
VENKAIAH NAIDU): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) The Ministry of Rural Developmen t regularly convenes Meetings 
with the State/UT Authorities and arra nge Workshops with Project Directors 
of the Districts Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) to review progress of 
the programmes including the Indira Aw as Yojana (IAY). For this purpose, 
the Minister of Rural Development ha s visited several States in recent 
months and held discussions with the Chief Ministers and other authorities. 
The Ministry also obtains Annual and Monthly Progress Report from all the 
States/UTs in this regard and Area Officers of the Ministry have been 
designated to undertake field visits, hold ; review meetings and ascertain the 
status of implementation of various Rural Development Programmes, in 
order that any bottlenecks being encountered are speedily removed. 
(b) to (d) As per the information r eceived from the Government of 
Gujarat, about 16,578 houses were constructed upto 28th February, 2001, 
against a target of 17,295 fpr the construction of new

houses in the State under the I AY for the year 2000-2001. The latest 
information indicates that the target for the year 2000-2001 under the IAY has

*467. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: W ill the Minister of TEXTILES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have issued any fresh guidelines for 
implementing the provisions of Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory use of 
Packing Commodities) Act, 1987; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government have receive d any complaints regarding the 
violation of provisions made under the said Act; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by Government to implement the provisions made in 
the fiscal Act? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI KASHI RAM RANA): (a) to (e) A 
statement is laid on the table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The Government has not issued any fresh guidelines for 
implementing the provisions of Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory use of 
Packing Commodities) Act, 1987. However, Government has issued a 
Notification under section 3 of Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory use of 
Packing Commodities) Act, 1987 on 25.10.2000 for the jute year 2000-2001. 
The notification stipulates 100% foodgrains & Sugar and 20% of urea to be 
packed in

Jute Packaging Material. The order provides for a relaxation upto a maximum

5 Kg. are exempted in respect of foodgrains and sugar. 
(c) and (d) The Government has not received any reports regarding the 
violation of provisions made under the said Act except slippages in the 
fertilizer sector. 
(e) In order to secure compliance of the Order, Jute Commissioner's 
office is monitoring the use of jute bags by the specified sectors under Jute

Powers under Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory use of Packing 
Commodities) Act, 1987 have been delegated to Chief Director (Sugar), 
Ministry of Consumer Affairs & Public Distribution and to Executive 
Director, Department of Fertiliser to monitor enforcement of jute packaging 
in sugar and fertilizer sector respectively.

Relief and rehabilitation for the victims of militancy In Jammtf and 
Kashmir 
*468. MIRZA ABDUL RASHID: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the victims of militancy in Jammu and Kashmir and 
displaced people of border areas are covered by relief and rehabilitation 
schemes of his Ministry; 
(b) if so, what has been done by Government for their relief and 
rehabilitation; and 
(c) whether Government have any plans to set-up orphanages aid and 
special treatment centres for innumerable orphaned, widowed and maimed 
victims of the proxy war? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME 
AFFAIRS (SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYASAGAR RAO); (a) to (c) 
Relief is a State subject and the G overnment of J&K has been providing ex-
gratia relief to the victims of militancy for death, injury, etc. As per the 
existing rules of the State Government, Rs. 1 lakh is paid to the next-of-kin 
in case of death, Rs. 75,00(y-, Rs. 5000 /- and Rs. l,0OQ /- for permanent 
disability, grievous injury and minor injury respectively caused in a terrorist 
incident. Also 50% of the loss of immovable property subject to a ceiling of 
Rs. 2 lakhs, is paid as compensation to the person whose property is 
damaged. The expenditure incurred by the State Government in this regard is 
reimbursed by this Ministry under Security Related Expenditure. A sum of 
Rs. 265.30 crores has been reimbursed to the State Government till the end of 
January 2001 against payment of ex-gratia relief to the next-of-kin of those 
killed as well as to those injured and compensation for damagedoss of 
property during the period of militancy in the State since 1990. 
With the objective of providing assistance for psychological and economic 
rehabilitation of the victims of militancy, the State Government of Jammu & 
Kashmir had set up a Council in 1995 for rehabilitation of widows, orphans, 
handicapped and old-aged persons adversely affected by militancy. It also 
aims at better coverage of 
39 

RAJYA SABHA [18 April, 2001] 
beneficiaries under various on-going welfare and development schemes of the 
Government. As a registered body under the Societies Registration Act, it 
functions as a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO). The Council has a 
corpus fund of Rs. 20 crores against which a sum of Rs. 6 crores has been 
contributed by the Central Government. In view of the magnitude of the tasks 
involved, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment has been requested to 
engage some NGOs in the rehabilitation of children orphaned by militancy 
particularly in the Kashmir Valley. 
For persons displaced for border area s, a relief package consisting of 
free ration, clothing, temporary acco mmodation, free medical check-up and 
financial assistance for replacement of destroyed houses and livestock was 
approved by Ministry of Home Affairs and was announced by the State 
Government in July 1999. It was revi sed in August 1999. Initially, the relief 
package was announced for period of 10 months from August 1999 to May 
2000. Later, the relief was extende d till 31st March 2001. The total 
expenditure envisaged was Rs. 58.21 crores against which Rs. 57.80 crores 
stands released (Rs. 37.80 crores from NDF and Rs. 20 crores from SRE). 
While all the displaced persons have returned to their homes, about 
11044 families from the border villages of Khour and Akhnoor tehsils of

way police can check whether arms purchased through it is for a genuine

weapons? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME 
AFFAIRS (SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYASAGAR RAO): (a) to (c) 
Licence for arms & ammunition is granted by the Licencing Branch of Delhi 
Police after verification of the character and antecedents of applicants and 
assessing the need and desirability for possession of a fire arm. The same 
procedure is followed at the time of renewal of the licence. Subsequent to the 
issue of licence and purchase of wea pon, the particulars of the licencee and

police to enable the weapons so licen sed to be physically inspected from 
time to time. The cases in which involvement of the licencee or the licensed 
arm in commission of heinous crime comes to the notice of the local police, 
the licence is immediately suspended or cancelled. In such cases weapon is 
deposited with the nearest Police Station to prevent its further misuse. During 
the year 1999 and upto 15.3.2001, Delhi Police issued 56 show cause notices 
for cancellation of arms licences and cancelled licences in five cases.

Sick coal mines in the country 
3487. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Mi nister of COAL be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have identified the sick coal mines in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the location thereof Company-wise;

the public sector coal companies; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
70 

[18 April, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(e) the steps taken thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COAL (SHRI 
SYED SHAHNAWAZ HUSSAIN): (a) and (b) Under the provisions of the 
Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985, when the net-worth 
of a coal company becomes negative, the company becomes a sick company. 
There is no provision regarding any individual mine becoming sick. Eastern 
Coalfields Limited (ECL) had a negative net-worth as on 31.3.99 and was 
referred to BIFR under the aforesaid Act. The BIFR have declared the 
company as sick. The Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) had also a 
negative net-worth as on 31.3.2000 an d the company has been referred to 
BIFR under the ACT. These two companies are incurring losses because they 
have a number of heavily losing mines. In ECL & BCCL most of the loss 
making mines are located in the State of Jharkhand. 
(c) to (e) The Coal India Limite d has engaged ICICI to study the 
problems of ECL and BCCL, the loss- making subsidiaries of CIL, and to 
make recommendations for their revival. In case of Central Coalfields 
Limited, another loss making coal company, the EDBI has been engaged to 
study the problems and make recommendations for its revival. The report of 
ICICI on ECL has been received, whereas the reports on BCCL and CCL 
have not so far been received. The ICICI REPORT ON ECL has been 
examined but no final revival package has so far been formulated.

Fake currency notes 
3500. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P. GOYAL: Will the Minister of 
HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that fake currency notes 
are present in large quantities posing a threat to our economy; 
(b) if so, what steps are being taken by Government to curb fake 
currency notes; 
(c) whether any pattern has been established regarding their 
distribution, seizures and persons held possessing/dealing in fake currency 
notes; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether Nepal is becoming hub of these activities; and 
(f) whether any proposal/plan exist to deal with it effectively? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME 
AFFAIRS (SHRI I.D. SWAMI): (a), (c) and (d) Cases of circulation/seizure 
of fake currency notes are reported from time to time from various parts of 
the country. However, the recovery/ seizure of fake currency notes is 
marginal in comparison to the total currency in circulation. Available 
information indicates that fake Indian currency notes are being clandestinely 
inducted into the country from across the Indo-Pak border and Indo-Nepal 
border, besides being fabricated in India through a variety of techniques 
involving the use of printing presses, colour photocopiers, scanners and 
colour printers. 
(b) 'Police' and 'Public order' are State subjects as per the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution of India and, as such, registration,   
investigation,   detection   and   prevention   of   crimes 
84 

[18 April, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
including cases of counterfeit currency is primarily the responsibility 
of the State Governments.  However, the Union Government has taken the 
following steps: 
(i) The Central Bureau of Investigation has created a special unit for 
exclusive investigation of counterfeit currency notes. The Border 
Security Force has alerted its forward troops to be more vigilant so 
as to ensure that such currency notes are not smuggled into the 
country. 
(ii) A High Level Committee has be en constituted with representations 
from the Department of Economic Affairs, Reserve Bank of India, 
Ministry of Home Affairs/National Security Council Secretariat, to 
go into the entire gamut of issues pertaining to the circulation of 
fake Indian currency. 
(iii) A six-member Fact Finding Committee was set up under the 
convenorship of Shri V.K. Gaik wad, Dy. General Manager, RBI, 
comprising experts on note-printing/currency paper etc. for 
examining the fake notes seized in the past in order to enable the 
Government to take remedial action vis-a-vis printing and security 
features. The Committee has submitted its report, which is under 
examination. 
(iv) RBI has been advised to go in for a publicity campaign about 
security features incorporated in the genuine notes. 
The Reserve Bank of India has taken the following steps: 
(i) The security features of Rs.500 denomination notes has been widely 
publicized in the print media to help the people detect fake notes. 
(ii) A film on security features of Rs.500 denomination notes produced 
in English, Hindi and other regional languages has been telecast on 
Doordarshan. 
(iii) For the benefit of public, a booklet has been brought out which 
inter-alia, describes the features of genuine notes. This booklet 
has been placed on the RBI website besides being available to the 
public for sale at RBI's issue offices. 
85

with His Majesty's Government of Nepal. Both the sides have expressed 
determination to take urgent necessary steps to prevent the misuse of

the Pakistani Embassy in Kathmandu was caught on January 2, 2000 while

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRY OF POWER 
(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) and (b) A major grid disturbance 
resulted in the collapse of Northern Regional Grid on 2nd January, 2001 
causing inconvenience and loss due to disruption of railway traffic and loss 
of production in industrial units. Several factors contributed to the grid 
collapse. One pole of Rihand-Dadri HVDC line was out of service from 14th

number of 220 KV and 400 KV lines of UP transmision system had tripped

transmission capability which had been impaired due to reeduced capability 
of the Rihand-Dadri HVDC line got further eroded due to tripping of major 
high voltage lines in UP system and this triggered grid separation and 
collapse.

DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SHRIMATI) RrTA VERMA]: (a) and (b) No, Sir.

DEVELOPMENT [DR. (SHRIMATI) RITA VERMAj: (a) and (b) As per
